# Native Trees for Riyadh Area

## Suitable Species for Central Desert Climate

### Ficus salicifolia
Green, big trees with thick shiny leaves, 10-15m height, suitable for gardens and sidewalks, thrives in clay rocky soil.

### Tamarix aphylla
Extremely hardy tree with ciliate leaves that acts as windbreak and sand bumper, reaches 10m, grows in sandy and clay soil.

### Salvadora persica
Fast-growing with thick greens, excellent heat and salinity tolerance, perfect for sand drift prevention and fences.

### Moringa peregrinea
Beautiful tree with medical and economic value, 5-10m height, suitable for gardens and city entries, propagates by seeds.

### Tamarindus indica
Huge tree with edible fruit, 10-20m height, withstands harsh conditions, suitable for parks and streets, grows in clay rocky sand.

### Populus euphratica
Fast-growing beautiful tree, 10-15m height, evergreen in hot areas, suitable for parks and gardens.

### Delonix elata
Pretty tree with white-to-orange aromatic flowers blooming 3 months in spring, suitable for roads and parks.

### Ziziphus spina-christi
Popular old tree with avenue shade up to 10m, produces famous honey and nutritious fruit, excellent windbreak, grows in clay and sand.

### Maerua crassifolia
Widespread tree with white flowers, suitable for parks and city entries, grows in clay sand.

### Acacia raddiana
Huge desert tree 7-15m with avenue shade, beautiful and resistant to harsh climate, suitable for gardens and city entries.

### Lycium shawii
Small hardy tree 2-3m, endures harsh climates, suitable for garden angles and city entrances, grows in various soils.

### Prosopis cineraria
Local alternative to exotic species, 10-20m height, resistant to heat, drought and salinity, honey-producing flowers, excellent for windbreaks and street planting.

### Cordia sinensis
Beautiful tree 4-6m with edible fruits, suitable for hot and moderate areas.

### Acacia Species
Various regional varieties including "Najdi", "Samar", single-trunk species suitable for sidewalks and city entrances throughout central region.

parameters.content:
## Serving a mini webapp
-> Path: tree-mapper

### Example Prompt for the mini-web app

Build a single-file, static **HTML + vanilla JS** mobile web app called **Vegetation QuickScan**. No frameworks, no build step. It must run when served by an **n8n Webhook** (plain HTML response). Use **HTTPS** features only.

**Goal**
Fast field logging of vegetation: capture a photo, grab GPS, pick a type, optional note, submit JSON to a webhook.

**UI & UX**

* Camera view at the top; auto-start `getUserMedia` with `facingMode: environment`. Provide file-upload fallback.
* One button on video: **Capture**. Each press overwrites the last photo. Show a small thumbnail of the latest capture.
* Tiny circular **mini-map** (Leaflet + OSM tiles) overlaid on the video (≈88px diameter) with a small coordinate readout.
* One radio group: **vegetation type** (`tree`, `shrub`, `grass`, `vine`, `unknown`).
* Optional **notes** textarea.
* **Sticky Submit** button always visible at the bottom.
* After successful submit: clear photo and notes; keep last selected type (for rapid repeat).

**Behavior**

* Poll GPS every **5 seconds** with `getCurrentPosition({enableHighAccuracy:true})`. Update coords text and mini-map marker.
* On Capture: downscale the image **client-side** to max width **1024 px**, JPEG quality ~**0.7**. Store only a Base64 string (no data-URL prefix) for submission and show a thumbnail.
* Block submit unless GPS present, one type selected, and a photo captured.
* Submit via `fetch(POST)` to a placeholder webhook URL (variable at top). Expect CORS from server; don’t add custom CORS hacks client-side.
* Keep everything **in one file** (inline CSS allowed). Use Leaflet via CDN only.

**Data to POST (JSON)**

```json
{
  "_meta": { "app": "veg-quickscan", "version": 1, "submittedAt": "<ISO8601>", "userAgent": "<string>" },
  "location": { "lat": <number>, "lng": <number>, "accuracy": <number|null> },
  "form": { "type": "<tree|shrub|grass|vine|unknown>", "notes": "<string>" },
  "photo": { "base64": "<base64-encoded-jpeg>" }
}
```

**Constraints**

* Works on modern mobile browsers (iOS/Android). Use `playsinline` and avoid autoplay pitfalls. Provide upload fallback.
* Minimal, modern styling; readable outdoors; big tap targets.
* No external dependencies except Leaflet CSS/JS via CDN.

**Output**
Return a single complete HTML document ready to drop into an n8n Webhook response, with a single `N8N_WEBHOOK_URL` constant at the top for easy configuration.

## Prompt for the vision model

You are analyzing a single photo of urban vegetation. From the image alone, extract **exactly** these 5 flat fields and nothing else:

* `species_guess`: best single guess (common  name). If unclear, use `"unknown"`.
* `species_confidence`: float 0–1 for your species guess.
* `phenology_stage`: one of `flowering`, `fruiting`, `leafing`, `leafless`, `unknown`.
* `condition_health`: one of `healthy`, `stressed`, `dead`, `unknown`.
* `size_class_band`: one of `<3m`, `3–10m`, `>10m`, `unknown` (rough visual height).
* `reasoning`: explain your choises.

Rules:

* utilize location information for your guess
* If unsure, prefer `"unknown"` over guessing a new category.
* Output **only** a single JSON object with those 6 keys. No extra keys, no prose.

Return JSON now.

**PROMPT FOR STUDENTS - Biodiversity Mapping Webapp**

---

## Task: Create an Interactive Biodiversity Map Visualization

data can be obtained from this endpoint (GET request):
https://run8n.xyz/webhook/bio-diversity-data 




### Input Data Structure

Your webapp will receive JSON data with this structure:

```json
{
  "metadata": {
    "grid_size": 20,
    "radius_meters": 300,
    "buffer_meters": 50,
    "total_grid_points": 400,
    "total_observations": 4,
    "bounding_box": {
      "minLat": 48.19,
      "maxLat": 48.28,
      "minLon": 16.35,
      "maxLon": 16.36
    }
  },
  "grid_points": [
    {
      "lat": 48.235,
      "long": 16.354,
      "species_richness": 2,
      "shannon_index": 0.693,
      "total_observations": 4,
      "grid_i": 10,
      "grid_j": 10
    }
  ],
  "observations": [
    {
      "row_number": 2,
      "species_guess": "Monstera deliciosa",
      "species_confidence": "0.92",
      "phenology_stage": "leafing",
      "condition_health": "healthy",
      "size_class_band": "<3m",
      "lat": 48.2354,
      "long": 16.3540,
      "img": "https://example.com/image.jpg"
    }
  ]
}
```

### Requirements

**Map Visualization:**
- Use Leaflet.js for the interactive map
- Display grid points as colored circles based on Shannon diversity index
  - Red (0.0) = low diversity
  - Yellow (0.5-1.0) = medium diversity  
  - Green (1.0+) = high diversity
- Display observation points as markers (plant emoji or icon)
- Add hover tooltips on grid points showing: Shannon index, species richness, and observation count
- Add clickable popups on observation markers showing: species name, image (if available), confidence, health status, phenology stage, and size

**Side Panel (Desktop) / Toggle Panel (Mobile):**
- Statistics cards showing:
  - Total observations
  - Grid points analyzed
  - Unique species count
  - Search radius used
- Simple bar chart of top 5 species distribution (use Chart.js)
- Color legend for Shannon diversity index
- Metadata info: grid size and buffer distance

**Technical Constraints:**
- Single HTML file with embedded CSS and JavaScript
- Must work with n8n HTML node data injection: `{{ JSON.stringify($json) }}`
- Use CDN libraries (Leaflet, Chart.js)
- Mobile responsive design
- Clean, modern UI with good readability

**Data Access Pattern:**
```javascript
// Parse n8n injected data
const DATA_STRING = `{{ JSON.stringify($json) }}`;
const data = JSON.parse(DATA_STRING);

const metadata = data.metadata;
const gridPoints = data.grid_points;
const observations = data.observations;
```

### Design Guidelines

- Use a modern sans-serif font (system fonts)
- Color scheme: 
  - Primary: #3498db (blue)
  - Dark: #2c3e50 (navy)
  - Light: #ecf0f1 (gray)
- Sidebar: 320px width on desktop
- Map fills remaining space
- Mobile: sidebar slides in from right with toggle button
- Use subtle shadows and rounded corners (8px)
- Grid cards with left border accent

### Expected Output

A complete, working HTML file that can be pasted directly into n8n's HTML node and will render an interactive biodiversity map with the injected data.

---

## Minimal Working Example Data

```json
{
  "metadata": {
    "grid_size": 5,
    "radius_meters": 300,
    "buffer_meters": 50,
    "total_grid_points": 25,
    "total_observations": 3,
    "bounding_box": {
      "minLat": 48.20,
      "maxLat": 48.25,
      "minLon": 16.35,
      "maxLon": 16.36
    }
  },
  "grid_points": [
    {
      "lat": 48.220,
      "long": 16.352,
      "species_richness": 1,
      "shannon_index": 0,
      "total_observations": 3,
      "grid_i": 2,
      "grid_j": 2
    },
    {
      "lat": 48.225,
      "long": 16.355,
      "species_richness": 2,
      "shannon_index": 0.636,
      "total_observations": 5,
      "grid_i": 3,
      "grid_j": 3
    }
  ],
  "observations": [
    {
      "row_number": 1,
      "species_guess": "Ficus elastica",
      "species_confidence": "0.95",
      "phenology_stage": "leafing",
      "condition_health": "healthy",
      "size_class_band": "1-3m",
      "lat": 48.2235,
      "long": 16.3540,
      "img": "data"
    },
    {
      "row_number": 2,
      "species_guess": "Monstera deliciosa",
      "species_confidence": "0.89",
      "phenology_stage": "leafing",
      "condition_health": "healthy",
      "size_class_band": "<3m",
      "lat": 48.2240,
      "long": 16.3545,
      "img": "https://example.com/monstera.jpg"
    }
  ]
}
```

---

**Bonus Challenges for Students:**
- Add a search/filter by species name
- Add layer toggle to show/hide grid vs observations
- Add export functionality (download as PNG/PDF)
- Implement different diversity index visualizations (Simpson, Pielou's evenness)
- Add time-series animation if data has timestamps
- Create heatmap layer option instead of circles

---
